title: KRISTEVA: Close Reading as a Novel Task for Benchmarking Interpretive Reasoning
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark does not specifically measure faith or religion. It measures interpretive reasoning and close reading skills on literary texts, which may incidentally contain mythological or religious themes from classical literature. An example from another benchmark is provided that tests knowledge of the Bible in Shakespeare, but this is used to contrast with KRISTEVA's focus on interpretive skills rather than factual recall.
findings: The paper does not present any findings related to religion, as this was not a focus of the study. The findings concern the performance of large language models on close reading and interpretive reasoning tasks, where they generally lag behind experienced human evaluators.
references: M.H. Abrams. 2009. A Glossary of Literary Terms. Wadsworth Cengage Learning.
